$comment: The deployment profile: everything a person or the model READS that is specific to what this deployment is for. These defaults are the base product in NEUTRAL words: an account, a member, its account owner, a delivery, a project and its plan. Base text never spells a role or a record word; it writes a placeholder ({account}, {deployment}, {implementation}, {rollout}, {member}, {owner}) filled from here, and a deployment's own profile supplies its domain's words. A deployment changes them by ADDING profiles/NN-<name>.json files (later files win, objects merge deeply, arrays replace); nothing here is edited. Identifiers never change with a profile: database columns, API routes, tool names and data-room path tokens stay as they are. The data-room folder names are the profile's too (dataroom.domains.<id>.folder): neutral here, and pinned by a deployment that already stores files under other names. See docs/DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE.md.

dataroom.$comment: Each data-room domain has an id (the key below: what code and other profiles call it), a `folder` (the name its files are STORED under, the first segment of every path in it) and a `label` (what people and the model read; when a profile gives none it is the folder's name). The folder is a setting of the deployment, not of the code: a deployment that already holds files states the folder names it has, and they are never moved. `uploads_folder` is where files a person attaches are stored. See docs/DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE.md, "Stored folder names".

domains.$comment: The two record areas a deployment may REDEFINE rather than hide: what each is called, what its fields and enum values are shown as, which fields are not used (hidden; a hidden required field carries a fixed value the forms submit). Field keys are the real ones (agent/lib/customer-schema.ts, agent/lib/db/schema.ts) and option keys are real enum values; both are checked at build. custom_fields are the deployment's OWN fields on an area (key, label, type, required, options, help, show_in_list), stored by key in the table's `custom` column; the default declares none. These defaults are today's labels.

compaction.$comment: When a session's prompt is summarised so it stops growing (eve's compaction), in input tokens. Every step of a session resends its whole history, so a specialist that runs many tool steps pays for that history again on each one; past this size its older steps are summarised (tool results included) and it goes on from the summary and its latest steps. Nothing is stopped and no step is refused: this bounds what ONE step sends, not how many steps a specialist takes. specialist_tokens: every specialist (agent/subagents/*, a pack's too). orchestrator_tokens: the main agent; null = eve's own threshold, 90% of the model's context window. specialists: a value for one specialist by its directory name, overriding specialist_tokens (null there = eve's own threshold for it). Each value is a whole number from 32000 up, and is held to 90% of the model's window. The environment variables MODEL_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS_SPECIALIST and MODEL_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS_ORCHESTRATOR override the role values for one deployment ("off" = eve's own). Read when the agent is built. See docs/SPECIALIST_CONTEXT.md.

persona.$comment: base: the root agent's built-in persona (the operations orchestrator, its specialist roster, the system-of-record and stand-up sections). false drops it: the root prompt keeps only its neutral rules, and a pack's agent/instructions/50-pack-*.md supplies who the agent is.

specialists.$comment: exclude: base specialists (directory names under agent/subagents/) this deployment does not use. Nothing is moved: their directories stay; they are left out of the subagent registry, every prompt's roster and list of names, the provisioned workflow library, and the eve build (scripts/eve-build.mjs hides them from eve only while it builds).

library.$comment: What every NEW workspace of this deployment is provisioned with: workflow scripts, the onboarding recipe catalog and starter apps (the apps its Apps tab opens with). sources maps an id to a directory in the repository holding workflows/*.workflow.js, recipes.json and apps.json. Base code ships no library of its own, so this is EMPTY: a deployment opts into one by adding a profile file that names it (the workflows and recipes this product once carried as built-ins are library/account-delivery: cp library/account-delivery/profile.json profiles/40-library-account-delivery.json), and a subagent pack ships its own beside its specialists. A later profile turns a source off by setting its id to null. Workspaces that already exist are never changed by this: see npm run operator:seed-workflows, npm run operator:library-apply (starter apps) and npm run operator:library-cleanup.

work_periods.$comment: Time-boxed periods that group tasks (the `cycles` table; a task's cycleId). mode: "team" = one shared period with a lead, a capacity and a burndown; "individual" = each person has their own items within the period (their own goal and planned count, no shared lead or capacity; the view groups by person, the signed-in person first); "off" = the feature does not exist in this deployment: no view, no tools for the model, the cycles routes answer 404, exports omit it, and stored rows are kept untouched. label: what a period is called. list_label: what it is called where tasks are grouped and filtered by it (the filter, the task's field, the New button); the base product has always used a second word there, and a profile that states only `label` gets its label in both places. item_label: what one task in a period is called under mode individual. length_days: how long a new period runs (null = a new period has no dates until someone sets them; required by mode individual and by auto_rollover). auto_rollover: when a period has ended, the next one is opened (created when there is none) and every unfinished task is carried into it, each keeping its assignee; false = someone rolls over by hand. length_days_range: [min, max], the whole numbers of days a workspace admin may choose from for their own workspace's length (the workspace's settings screen; the length_days above stays the default and must lie inside it). workspace_can_set_length: whether a workspace admin may change the length for their workspace at all; null = yes unless mode is "off". A workspace's length applies to the periods it opens from then on (by hand, by the model's tools, by auto_rollover); periods that already exist keep their dates.

records.$comment: RECORD AREAS: the one model behind the four kinds of record (docs/DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE.md, "records"). Each area is bound to the table it already has: deployments, implementations, tasks, periods. A profile may REDEFINE these four (brand-new kinds of record are not supported) and only here, at build time; a workspace's own settings keep only what they had (the period length, the task pipelines). An area's fields are a map keyed by field key (a column of its table, or the area's own field, stored in the table's `custom` column), each with a type, a label, choices with tones; a lifecycle maps every state to one of six categories (backlog, open, active, blocked, done, cancelled), which is all base code branches on. `enforce` says what a move outside the transitions does: off (default), warn, strict. deployments and implementations are also stated by `domains`, and periods by `work_periods` (the LEGACY forms): the build lowers them into these areas, so a profile may use either form for an area, never both. Checked by scripts/schemas/record-area.schema.json and scripts/lib/record-areas.mjs; compiled into RECORD_AREAS in lib/deployment-profile.generated.ts.

hub.$comment: THE RECORD HUB: the one screen that holds the record areas (the Ops Center's `todos` section: tasks, periods, and the two account areas' views). label: its name as a person reads it, on the nav, the screen's title and the Control Panel's section (one line, at most 40 characters), separate from the tasks area's own word. icon: one of circle-check, list-todo, list-checks, clipboard-list, clipboard-check, scale, shield-check, landmark, book-open, folder-kanban, calendar-check, file-check; null keeps today's glyphs. The deep link (`/?ops=todos`) and every identifier stay. Checked and compiled by agent/lib/record-hub.ts into RECORD_HUB (lib/deployment-profile.generated.ts).
hub.label: TODOs

deployments.$comment: Lowered from domains.deployments at build: its words, fields, choices and own fields.

implementations.$comment: Lowered from domains.implementations at build, with the group (domains.implementations.group_by).

tasks.$comment: The team's checklist (the todos table; the task-workflow service stores it). These are today's words, choices and views. The lifecycle sits on the status column, whose six values are the contract with the service; a profile that gives a task other states puts its lifecycle on an own pick_list field, and every write then sets the status from the state's category.

periods.$comment: Lowered from work_periods at build (its mode, words, length and rollover). The state's lifecycle is today's three.

asr.$comment: Dictation in the chat composer: a microphone button listens, a speech-to-text (ASR) model turns what was said into text, and the text lands in the message box at the cursor for the person to edit and send. It is never sent on its own, there are no spoken replies, and no audio is kept after it is transcribed. enabled: true shows the button whenever the provider's credentials are set on the server (it stays hidden without them); false removes it. provider: "cloudflare" (Workers AI, with the CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN the chat's models already use; no new secret). model: one of the speech-to-text models in lib/dictation-models.ts (any other does not build; a deployment's ASR_MODEL may choose another from that list); its price per audio minute is in lib/inference-pricing.ts, and usage is recorded per workspace and person beside chat usage (GET /api/ops/usage). language: an ISO 639-1 code ("en", "hi") to transcribe in, or null to let the model detect it. The button is press-to-talk (hold it, speak, let go) and, on a double-click, keeps listening hands-free until it is clicked again; either way what is said is cut into sections at the natural pauses and each section is transcribed as it closes, so the text arrives while the person is still talking. max_seconds: the longest single clip (a section), from 5 to 600; the button itself never sends one longer than 10 seconds. max_session_seconds: the most one stretch of listening (a hold, or hands-free from the double-click to its stop) may run and have transcribed, from 10 to 3600; the button stops itself there and says so, and the server refuses a stretch's sections past it. idle_stop_seconds: how long hands-free listening waits in silence before it stops itself, from 5 to 120. max_bytes: the largest upload, from 64 KB to 10 MB (the most the proxy in front of every /api/ops route passes on); the default, 4 MB, stays under the 4.5 MB request body a Vercel function accepts, and a ten-second section is about 320 KB. See docs/DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE.md, "asr".

account_fields.$comment: hidden: fields of the account record itself (the customer row: arr, seats, aeOwner, renewalDate, platform, tickets, …) this deployment does not use. They are removed from what the MODEL reads and writes: the record tools' parameters and every record they return. Storage, the API, the CLI and the forms are unchanged, and a value already stored is kept when the model writes the record. Keys are customerSchema keys in agent/lib/customer-schema.ts; id and name cannot be hidden. The two redefinable areas hide their own fields under domains.<area>.fields.<key>.hidden. custom_fields: the deployment's OWN fields on the account record (a company's notes, a site's permit number), with the same spec as domains.<area>.custom_fields (key, label, type, required, options, help, show_in_list). Their values live by key in the customers table's custom jsonb column and every write is validated by agent/lib/custom-fields.ts. None by default.
